title: A backwater valve protects a drain, not the drinking-water supply
description: Identify the sewer backwater valve, understand what it can and cannot stop, and avoid confusing it with a potable-water backflow preventer.
prompt: Is the problem on a drain or sewer line?
answer: A backwater valve is a one-way drainage device intended to resist sewage flowing backward into a building. It is related by user language, but it is not the same product or compliance workflow as a potable-water backflow assembly.
urgency: Active sewage backup is a sanitation hazard. Avoid contact and use an emergency drain or plumbing service when wastewater is entering the building.
diagramAlt: Simplified sewer backwater valve with access lid and flapper
identifiers: It is installed in a building drain or sewer lateral, often behind an access cover.
It typically uses a flap or gate that closes against reverse wastewater flow.
It does not have test cocks or a potable-water utility test tag.

choices.label: Sewage is entering the building
choices.detail: Treat this as an urgent sanitation and drainage problem.

choices.label: The valve chatters or does not reopen
choices.detail: The access and drain condition need inspection; do not force the mechanism blindly.

choices.label: My notice is from the water utility
choices.detail: You may be looking for a potable-water backflow preventer instead.

steps.title: Confirm the pipe system
steps.body: Drain and sewer piping carries wastewater; potable supply piping feeds fixtures and irrigation.

steps.title: Find the access point
steps.body: A service cover near the building drain is a common backwater-valve clue.

steps.title: Separate cause from protection
steps.body: A backwater valve can resist reversal, but it does not remove a blockage or guarantee protection in every flood event.

safeChecks: Keep people and pets away from wastewater.
Photograph the access cover and surrounding floor level.
Note whether multiple fixtures are affected.
stopConditions: A stuck valve combined with ongoing fixture use
No safe access to the drain
notThisDevice: It is not an RPZ, PVB, or double-check assembly.
It does not satisfy a water-utility backflow testing notice.
It is not a pressure regulator.

related.title: Get help with an active problem

evidenceNote: This page deliberately separates sewer protection from drinking-water backflow compliance so the domain does not blur two different systems.
